classification.difficultyReason: All vectors are anchored at O, and the diagram plus the midpoint information scaffold the task. Part a is a doubling from the midpoint (OM to OA). Part b is a single path sum, AO + OB, with a sign reversal. Part c, the hardest part, takes two steps: halve OB to get ON, then go the route M to O to N, MO = -a and ON = 2b. This is more than the single path addition in p59-q3, because the student must use the midpoint relationships and reverse a vector. It is a little easier than p65-q25, which gives AC and BC (both pointing toward C) so the student must reverse directions, and which also needs a half-vector in AM. No coefficient comparison, ratio division or proof is required, so it stays routine linked procedures.
